evidence_decisions: The original table script controls runtime bindings; the factory manual controls physical devices and wiring. VPW is supplemental geometry with shared ancestry, not independent physical authority.

Mode sign: nine individual world-mesh bounds centres project LEDs 73-80; 80 has two. The old sign had a mis-scaled width 129.57 versus VPW 87.5, with plastic aspect ratio about 0.72 versus VPW 0.55. Its old y about 0.0345 differs from the new y about 0.0601. Factory board geometry and owner-photo front windows reconcile the rebuilt sign; these are table-specific geometry defects, not a general rejection of old runtime bindings.

Ten flash circuits each have one bulb: nine domes including the Comic Book Guy light and the Homer socket. The aggregate BOM count 13 does not establish additional bulbs on those circuits; render doubles are not physical sockets.

The mini TV is a physical 14x10 bicolor display on the playfield. LibPinMAME exposes its composite frame at index3 with width14 and height10; layout indices1/2 are the green/red CORE_NODISP planes of the same TV. The main 128x32 DMD is in the backbox.
Lamp 16 has two manual leader endpoints calibrated against 6 controls, with normalized uncertainty 0.02; one glow does not locate two sockets.

Backpanel has 10 physical sockets; the eight shared socket controls fit a 1D projective mapping. backwall_gion world mesh y=-4.0773VPU is just behind the modelled playfield bounds; factoryPDF121 and owner photographs put the sockets on the upright rear panel. Clamp its plane to y=0, disclose raw out-of-range value; no change to x from lightmap geometry.
The missing upper GI socket uses the factory underside-axis fit at (0.25, 0.01), with normalized uncertainty 0.01. The remaining matched table points retain their own coordinates.

Owner-photo fixed-camera triangulation locates the Homer socket holder and the GI5 replacement LED cap. The original incandescent filament is not visible; bulb axis, replacement body and camera model add systematic uncertainty beyond the perturbation interval.

HEP finished-build photos5/6 show a separate horizontal unhooded lamp under PARTY, between the reflector and right flipper. Its own replacement LED cap projects to (.69,.82), independently reproduced from four calibrated views. The factory location, circuit totals and unique laydown GI wedge holder reconcile the nominal F25 #555; contacts, wire colors and original filament are hidden. The camera/UV and replacement-filament allowance is .03 x/.02 y.

Public lamps 81-96 are not physical matrix circuits. The service test exercises 1-80, and the bounded ROM writer scan corroborates the disposition; neither a silent trace nor an extended-opcode-only scan proves no arbitrary indexed write.

gi.notes: One aggregate GI relay: Whitestar nGI=1 and the known-working UpdateGI script agree with the factory relay switching all four fused branches together (PDF121): F24 backpanel, F25 left playfield plus right return, F26 upper playfield plus five reflector spots and coin door, F27 right playfield. These are not four independently controllable strings. The reconciled physical layout has 26 main-floor #44 locations (25 physical socket anchors and the CBG factory-symbol projection), seven upper-playfield bayonets and ten rear-panel bayonets, plus five #555 reflector spots and the separate horizontal unhooded lamp under the PARTY right-return plastic: 49 playfield/rear emitters, all placed. Its #555/F25 association follows the factory location description, circuit totals and unique laydown GI wedge holder; the photograph does not expose the contacts or wire colors. Physical quantity 51 includes the two US coin-door #555 bulbs, which have no playfield coordinates; the European one-bulb coin door gives 50. This quantity describes the retained physical layout, not a universal production invariant. PDF121 nominally lists 40 GI #44 and six non-cabinet #555; PDF90's 45 total #44 minus four matrix #44 implies 41 GI bayonets, while the reconciled #44 locations total 43. The socket rows likewise sum to 45 (19 staple-down + four laydown + 22 long-shell), two fewer than the 47 #44 locations including the matrix. The factory explicitly warns GI quantities may change during production. The photo-confirmed extra rear-floor sockets are retained instead of deleting physical hardware to fit either nominal count. GI030/GI053 coincide with the mini-flipper shafts and are excluded; GI040/GI043 are one socket, not two. GI032 and GI31 mark flasher/spotlight wiring passages, not bulbs. The older 42-member render collection is not a physical inventory. Upper missing socket and backpanel coordinates are calibrated factory/photo projections with .01 normalized uncertainty. The separate left and right-return sockets use their own flat texture annuli with .02 allowance; the fourth left-return socket uses .01. The CBG-area GI uses the factory bulb-symbol projection at (.17,.32), with .05 schematic allowance per axis, not a photographed filament. Four reflector axes use conditional #555 filament projections with .02 allowance, and the fifth uses a replacement LED-cap projection with .01 allowance. The PARTY lamp uses its own replacement LED body projection at (.69,.82), with .03 x/.02 y allowance for camera/UV assumptions, partial occlusion and original-filament displacement; it is not the V01 bayonet, reflector or GI31 wiring passage. Original incandescent filaments are not observed.
